description: Visualize Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Kafka) CloudWatch metrics: broker health, cluster health, topic throughput, and consumer lag.

panels.description: ActiveControllerCount: number of active controllers in the cluster — should always be 1; 0 or >1 signals a controller election problem. OfflinePartitionsCount: number of partitions with no active leader — should be 0; any value above 0 means those partitions are unavailable for reads/writes.
panels.title: Active Controller Count / Offline Partitions Count

panels.description: Shows the worst observed under-replicated / under-min-ISR partition count per period (Maximum), not a summed total across samples.
panels.title: Under-Replicated / Under Min-ISR Partitions by Broker

panels.description: Kafka data logs disk usage shown as peak (Maximum) per broker to catch near-full disk conditions early; App Logs and Root disk shown as Average.
panels.title: Disk Used (Data/App Logs/Root) by Broker

panels.description: CpuSystem + CpuUser + CpuIOWait per broker (Maximum), computed per fixed broker ID 1/2/3 for capacity-planning parity with the AWS console dashboard.
panels.title: Total CPU Utilization by Broker

panels.description: 1 - RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent per broker, using Maximum, for worst-case thread-pool utilization (capacity-planning parity with the AWS console dashboard).
panels.title: Request Handler Average Utilization by Broker

panels.description: Memory Used shown as peak (Maximum) per broker to catch memory pressure spikes; Memory Free shown as Average.
panels.title: Memory Used / Memory Free by Broker

panels.description: MaxOffsetLag: highest offset lag (unconsumed messages) across all partitions for this consumer group/topic. SumOffsetLag: total offset lag summed across all partitions. Rising values mean the consumer group is falling behind producers.
panels.title: Consumer Lag (Max / Sum Offset Lag)

panels.description: CpuUser: % of CPU time spent in user space on the broker host. CpuSystem: % of CPU time spent in kernel/system space. CpuIdle: % of CPU time the host was idle. The three should sum to roughly 100%.
panels.title: CPU User / System / Idle by Broker

panels.description: RequestHandlerAvgIdlePercent: average % of time broker request-handler threads are idle — low values mean the broker is saturated handling requests. RequestThrottleTime: average time (ms) client requests were throttled by quota enforcement. RequestExemptFromThrottleTime: average time (ms) spent on requests exempt from throttling.
panels.title: Request Handler Idle % / Throttle Time / Exempt Time by Broker

panels.description: SwapUsed: swap space (bytes) used on each broker host. Sustained non-zero swap usage indicates memory pressure and can degrade broker performance.
panels.title: Swap Used by Broker

panels.description: MemoryCached / MemoryBuffered: memory (bytes) used by the OS page cache and buffers on each broker host. High cache usage is expected and normal since Kafka relies heavily on the OS page cache for throughput.
panels.title: Memory Cached / Memory Buffered by Broker

panels.description: GlobalPartitionCount: total number of partitions across the cluster. GlobalTopicCount: total number of topics across the cluster. Track these against your cluster's partition/topic limits to spot capacity risk.
panels.title: Global Partition Count / Global Topic Count

panels.description: LeaderCount: number of partitions this broker currently leads. PartitionCount: total partitions (leader + follower) hosted on this broker. Large imbalances across brokers indicate uneven partition/leader distribution.
panels.title: Leader Count / Partition Count by Broker

panels.description: Broker network throughput shown as peak (Maximum) per period, not a summed rate, to surface true throughput spikes.
panels.title: Network In / Out by Broker

panels.description: NetworkRxPackets: packets/sec received by the broker's network interface. NetworkTxPackets: packets/sec transmitted (plotted inverted for a mirrored view).
panels.title: Network Rx / Tx Packets by Broker

panels.description: NetworkRxDropped / NetworkTxDropped: packets/sec dropped on receive/transmit due to buffer exhaustion. NetworkRxErrors / NetworkTxErrors: packets/sec that failed due to network interface errors. These are host-level network issues, not Kafka protocol errors — non-zero values point to NIC or OS network saturation.
panels.title: Network Rx/Tx Dropped / Errors by Broker

panels.description: ReplicationBytesInPerSec: bytes/sec a broker receives from other brokers for partition replication (as a follower). ReplicationBytesOutPerSec: bytes/sec a broker sends to followers (as leader), plotted inverted for a mirrored view.
panels.title: Replication Bytes In / Out by Broker

panels.description: ZooKeeper request latency shown as p99 to surface tail latency rather than mean, which can hide spikes that stress the controller.
panels.title: ZooKeeper Request Latency / Session State

panels.description: MessagesInPerSec: number of messages produced per second into this topic, summed across its partitions/brokers.
panels.title: Messages In by Topic

panels.description: Topic-level throughput shown as peak (Maximum) per period, not a summed rate, to surface true throughput spikes per topic.
panels.title: Topic Bytes In / Out

panels.description: FetchMessageConversionsPerSec: rate of message-format down-conversions performed when serving fetch requests to older consumer clients. ProduceMessageConversionsPerSec: rate of format conversions performed on produce requests from older producer clients. Frequent conversions add broker CPU overhead and usually mean clients are on an outdated message format.
panels.title: Fetch / Produce Message Conversions by Topic

panels.description: ProduceMessageConversionsTime: average time (ms) the broker spends converting produced message formats for older-client compatibility. Sustained high values add CPU overhead.
panels.title: Produce Message Conversions Time by Topic

panels.description: EstimatedMaxTimeLag: estimated maximum time (seconds) for the consumer group to catch up on its most-lagging partition, based on recent consumption rate. EstimatedTimeLag: estimated time (seconds) per partition to reach the current offset — useful for understanding lag in time rather than offset count.
panels.title: Estimated Max / Current Time Lag by Consumer Group
